brief: RenderBrief(subject='A single small origami paper boat folded from greyish newsprint, its printed columns reduced to faint unreadable smudges of text, hull edges softened and slightly translucent where water has wicked upward; drifting along a shallow flooded city gutter, waterline lapping a submerged curb and drowned cobblestones; the boat shares the current with one drifting wet maple leaf and a slow swirl of fine silt; far behind, an out-of-focus row of rain-darkened storefronts and a leaning street sign dissolves into grey', motion="The boat rides the slow gutter current with near-weightless responsiveness: it bobs and dips on every micro-ripple, yaws a few degrees left then right like a compass needle, and its bow parts the water in a tiny laminar curl no wider than a fingernail; capillary action visibly darkens the paper's lower edge as the stain ring creeps upward; occasional drops from an unseen overhang strike the surface and send ring ripples that rock the boat and jostle the leaf; the paper skin flexes faintly with each bob; silt traces slow helical patterns beneath it", camera="Extreme macro, 100mm macro lens at roughly 1:2 magnification, camera float-mounted just above the waterline so the surface clips the lower frame edge; slow smooth lateral tracking move matching the boat's drift speed, keeping the hull in the near third; razor-thin depth of field with the curb and background storefronts melted into soft grey bokeh discs; one gentle rack focus from the waterline stain on the hull to a suspended droplet trembling on the boat's bow ridge; subtle handheld micro-sway as if the operator is crouched at the gutter's edge; specular sky reflections skimming the water as soft grey highlights", style='Overcast melancholy: flat silver-lead light from a full cloud deck, no cast shadows, everything lit by the sky itself; heavily desaturated palette of bleached newsprint whites, cold blue-grey water, wet charcoal stone, and one muted ochre note from the leaf; soft low-contrast film emulation in the character of Fuji Eterna with lifted blacks, fine 16mm grain structure, delicate wet-surface sheen, minimal halation with only a faint bloom on the brightest water glints; texture-forward — visible paper fibers, pulp swelling, silt suspension', audio_direction='Quiet interior-gutter soundstage: close, intimate water — small lapping against paper and stone, thin trickling current, irregular droplets striking the flood surface with soft plosive rings; a low sustained sub-bass room-tone of distant muffled city hum and far thunder rolling once; sparse melancholy tones — a single felt-piano note swelling mid-shot with a bowed low pad beneath; everything slightly wet-filtered, no sharp transients, dynamics kept hushed and close', negatives='no soft dissolves or morphs, no tearing or warping of the paper geometry, no boat unfolding or changing scale, no extra figures or hands entering frame, no text artifacts or legible lettering on the newsprint, no sudden weather change or sunlight breaking through, no water simulation flicker on the reflection highlights', identity_lock="the boat's exact folded geometry — pointed prow, twin peaked ends, flat deck fold; grey newsprint with faint smudged unreadable print; the creeping dark waterline stain on the hull; the single ochre maple leaf as the only warm accent; the submerged curb running parallel along frame left; consistent silver-grey overcast exposure and desaturated palette from first frame to last")
